correctedCritiques.con-divine-logic-dilemma: Strongest feature: The reply formulates a two-horn challenge testing whether divine guarantorship explains logical invariance, attaching adverse consequences to both alterability and inability to alter logic. Principal limitation: The dilemma is not exhaustive, because logical laws might necessarily express an unchanging divine nature, neither created nor externally imposed, so this third model requires evaluation. Live burden: The negative must explain why necessary-expression accounts redescribe rather than ground logical necessity, while the affirmative must show how divine nature supplies explanatory value without collapsing into arbitrariness or external constraint. Locked score: The very strong band recognizes precise structure, relevance, and interrogative calibration, moderated by incomplete charity toward the third option and no conclusive demonstration that every divine relationship fails.
correctedCritiques.con-perfect-ground-fallible-access: Strongest feature: The reply separates a perfect ontological foundation from fallible human access, showing divine existence cannot transmit maximal epistemic warrant through imperfect cognitive faculties. Principal limitation: The claim that God cannot provide assurance unless minds become unflawed exceeds demonstration, because generally reliable faculties, revelation, or defeasible authentication remain conceivable. Live burden: The affirmative must explain epistemic transmission from divine ground to human belief and calibrate promised warrant, while the negative must distinguish objections to maximal certainty from objections to ordinary fallible knowledge. Locked score: The very strong band recognizes a responsive, charitable, and powerful internal critique succeeding while granting the divine premise, moderated for overstating the impossibility of divine communication and overlooking reliable but imperfect access.
